name: Adaptive Out-of-Core Single-Pass GPU Raycasting
definition: An adaptive out-of-core technique for rendering massive scalar volumes employing single pass GPU raycasting. It decomposes a volumetric dataset into small cubical bricks organized into an octree structure maintained out-of-core. The octree contains original data at leaves and filtered representations of children at inner nodes. An adaptive loader on the CPU updates a view- and transfer function-dependent working set of bricks on GPU memory by asynchronously fetching data. A compact indexing structure spatially organizes the working set into an octree hierarchy encoded in a small texture, exploited by a stackless raycasting algorithm.
